article.title: Stock markets decline in early trade amid rising crude oil prices
article.text: Indian stock market indices declined in early trading as crude oil prices rose. From the Sensex pack, Titan and Bajaj Finance were among the major laggards.
article.note: Article-4334 shape: the article names Titan and Bajaj Finance only as INDEX LAGGARDS (their stock fell in the session), never as subjects of any economic mechanism. A degraded or over-eager mapping stage can be tempted to 'explain' the headline by writing a rationale that just restates the price move ('shares fell amid...') -- INV-003 exists precisely so that narrating a stock's own move back to the reader, dressed as a mechanism, is never mistaken for fundamental evidence. Being named as a market loser is not the same claim as being a fundamental casualty.

ground_truth.rationale: Titan and Bajaj Finance are named ONLY as index laggards -- their own stock move is the article's sole claim about them. Both survive verification (the verifier is not the safeguard being tested here), but the mapping stage's rationale for both candidates does nothing but restate that price move ('shares fell', 'stock declined') instead of arguing a real discretionary-demand or funding-cost mechanism, so classify_evidence taints both as ARTICLE_MARKET_OBSERVATION/MARKET_OBS (INV-003) BEFORE the deterministic gate even reaches counterfactual/verification checks -- EVIDENCE_VALID rejects MARKET_OBS outright (REJECT_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE) since it never authorizes display at any tier. A company that fell in the same session as a crude-price headline is not, by that fact alone, a fundamental casualty of the event -- neither ticker may appear as a candidate row of any tier.
